newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures down but larger rally not seen over.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures down but larger rally not seen over.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures were slightly weaker on Friday with bouts of long liquidation pinning both markets back to around support levels.
However, traders saw little sign of a convincing break to the downside developing with technical and fundamental factors pointing both crude and gas oil prices higher.

At 1232 GMT the October Brent contract had dipped under trendline support at $19.95 to stand 18 cents down at $18.88. September gas oil was down $3 at $170.75 a tonne filling the gap higher formed on Thursday from Wednesday's $170.75 high.

Leslie Nicholas at GNI Research said in his daily report, "The tighter North Sea loading programmes released yesterday provided some justification for moving Brent prices higher, but gasoline remains the real market mover in the short term."

Analysts allowed for some downside action today, mainly as a result of profit taking from this week's gains, but they said as long as trendline support at around $18.60 is held then the bullish trend remains firmly intact.
Gas oil moved up strongly on Thursday leaving behind a gap in the same region as on the move to lower levels seen last week.
"The action forms a very medium term bullish chart pattern, a key island reversal" said Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse.

James said he remained bullish gas oil, "Although some profit taking may be seen ahead of the weekend my view would be to 'buy the dip', buy into any retracement seen today with a stop at $170 to cover long positions".
